# VideoNook

> Video podcast and content studio in Armstrong, BC, Canada. Done-for-you weekly video reels and video podcast recording for business owners in the North Okanagan and Shuswap (Armstrong, Vernon, Salmon Arm, and surrounding communities).

VideoNook is a Rhythm Productions studio. Contact: info@rhythmproductions.ca. Website: https://videonook.ca

## Services and pricing

- We record your reels: $397/month (August 2026 special, regular $497/month). Done-for-you weekly video reels: 4 reels delivered monthly, a plan built around what your customers need to hear, scripting, monthly one-hour studio session, on-camera coaching, teleprompter available, editing, captions, post copy, and one round of revisions included. Monthly billing, three-month minimum, cancel anytime after.
- You record your reels: $197/month. A 30-minute studio session every month. Client brings the ideas and does the talking; VideoNook runs the camera, lights, and sound. Teleprompter available. Vertical single camera 1080p recording, raw files provided.
- Record your video podcast: $497/session. Up to 90 minutes in studio, up to 60 minutes recorded, two people. One horizontal 1080p video auto-cut live between 2 camera angles, audio baked in, plus a separate audio track for podcast platforms. Files delivered same day, when you leave. Extras: extra person +$50/seat (third seat with an additional camera, up to 3 cameras total), raw files +$97 (delivered in 48 business hours), 4K upgrade +$147 (raw files included, delivered in 48 business hours).
- Produced podcast episodes: starting at $997. Multicam edit, mixed audio, basic titles. One round of revisions.
- Prepaid 4-pack: $1,788 for 4 podcast recording sessions, use within 6 months.
- Podcast launch setup: $297 one time. Hosting platform setup, distribution to Spotify, Apple Podcasts, and YouTube, cover art in place.

## Key facts

- Studio location: Armstrong, BC (plenty of parking, easy highway access)
- Session hours: 9am to 5pm, Monday through Friday, by appointment only
- Service area: North Okanagan and Shuswap, including Vernon, Salmon Arm, and Armstrong
- All equipment included: cameras, mics, lighting, and an engineer
- Podcast recordings use two camera angles with engineered audio
